title: Draft: Stop capture based on data content - using display filters
description:
Instructions to use:
1. In the main GUI window, Apply a display filter that you want to
   trigger a capture stop. eg: `http contains "dylan"`
2. Select the interface
3. Capture -> Options... -> Options tab
4. Under "Stop capture automatically after...", select X number of
   "packets displayed in main GUI window", and check the box.
5. Start
6. Trigger the display filter to match. eg: Go to http://example.com/dylan
7. Capture stops

See: https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/15087

notes.body:
Remaining changes before I remove the 'Draft' status:
1. Make this work in tshark - Update the '-a' to add the additional case
2. Make this work in Wireshark.exe with '-a' too (if the commandline options are handled separately than tshark)
3. Add documentation, including limitations

I demo'd this to @rknall, and the main issue to address is tshark support.

What about making this feature more generic by letting the user configure a specific display filter to the stop condition? Doing this will let the user change main display filter while capturing using this option.

UI something like this:
```
Stop capture automatically after...
  [] X packets
    [] matching display filter: [     ]
  [] X files
  ...
```

The main benefit of not adding a 2nd display filter to trigger on, is that it would add a lot of complexity, and probably affect performance, because we're now running 2x separate checks.

Thinking more about this, the commandline version will be more useful for this use case, and it will be easier to use anyway. eg: `tshark -Y 'http contains "dylan"' -adisplayed_packets:1`
